lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Good morning Wesner! Thanks for picking up.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi, sorry, I'm in the car but I can talk.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How are you doing, really?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Good. Busy, but good.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay, good.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So did you manage to take a 10-minute walk after dinner on 4 days?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Some days yes, some days no. Maybe 1.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're open to it. You just want it to fit your real life.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: My kids is why I'm doing this. Some days are better than others.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If you don't do this, your health is going to suffer.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm too tired for this right now.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're not sure it's worth it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I feel better about myself when I stick to it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you think 5 days is realistic?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Not yet.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're weighing it up, and that's fair.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I guess.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Could someone in the family walk with you?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: No, not really. I'm going to do it Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is your daughter able to help?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Got it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, I think so.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's been a mixed week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: After dinner I can walk the dog, she needs it anyway.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you eat dinner at the same time every day?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Well, sometimes. After treatment I had no energy at all.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is that something you can do?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I see.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: No, not really. It rained almost every afternoon.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: The rain got in the way.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: If I plan it the night before, I can do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is your daughter able to help?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes. I already told my family about my goal.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So what would you like your goal to be for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: So, let's say I take a 10-minute walk after dinner on 3 days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Whatever you pick is fine with me. It's your plan.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What might get in the way?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll go to the mall instead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I'll text you midweek to see how it's going, and we'll talk again in two weeks.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Perfect.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Talk soon!

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thank you, talk soon.

tags.note: Family reason for change; coach did not explore
Warning about health; pushes without permission
Self-esteem benefit of sticking to plan
Plans night before; confidence to do it
Repeats question already asked at line 20
Names mall as barrier; not explored

flags.reason: Warns about health consequences right after participant named family motivation; pushes without permission.
Participant said 'I feel better about myself' (line 13); coach moved to a closed question instead of reflecting it.
Asks 'Is your daughter able to help?' again after the same question at line 20; repetitive questioning instead of exploring.
Participant named the mall as a barrier; coach moved on without exploring or planning around it.

score.summary: The coach used reasonable reflections and a closed-goal review, and the participant set a concrete 3-day walking goal with family support. However, the coach relied heavily on closed questions, gave an unsolicited health warning at line 10, and let change talk and the mall barrier pass without exploration.
strengths: Line 8 and line 16: complex reflections captured the participant's ambivalence well.
Line 36: 'It's your plan' supports autonomy in goal setting.
Line 39: clear next contact plan (midweek text and two-week follow-up).
coaching_tips: Line 10: replace the health warning with a question such as 'What would make this matter most to you?' to draw out the kids-related motivation.
Line 14 followed line 13: reflect the self-esteem change talk ('Sticking to it makes you feel good about yourself') before asking about goals.
Line 32: avoid repeating the line 20 question; try 'What would help you make the walks happen on those busy days?'
Line 38: explore the mall barrier with 'What could you do instead on a rainy day?' to build a concrete plan.
